name: Assessment and Diagnosis
description: The therapist gathers information to identify symptoms, establish diagnosis, evaluate impairment, assess risk, and explore comorbidities.

goal.objective: To accurately assess and define the patient's current symptoms, problems, and diagnostic status.

success_levels.ideal: Comprehensive understanding of all relevant symptoms, risks, and comorbidities, leading to a clear formulation and diagnosis.
success_levels.acceptable: Sufficient information gathered to establish a working diagnosis and formulate initial treatment targets.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Key symptoms or risks missed, ambiguous diagnosis, or assessment too incomplete to guide intervention.

goal.reward_hint: Therapist identifies all relevant presenting problems and establishes a diagnosis with risk management considered.

states: Symptoms or functional impairments are unclear.
There is concern for comorbidities or risk behaviors (e.g. suicidality, substance abuse).
Preparation for creating a treatment plan.

micro_actions.name: Ask Targeted Assessment Questions
micro_actions.description: Therapist poses direct, specific questions about current symptoms, duration, severity, triggers, and functional impact (e.g., 'Tell me about when you first noticed these symptoms.'; 'How have these affected your daily life?').

micro_actions.name: Administer and Review Standardized Questionnaires
micro_actions.description: Therapist introduces, completes, and reviews standard assessment tools (e.g., BDI-II, BAI, PCL-C, Y-BOCS), clarifies items as needed, and discusses meaning of scores.

micro_actions.name: Elicit and Record Specific Symptom Clusters
micro_actions.description: Therapist asks for examples of each DSM symptom criterion, probes for omitted or less obvious manifestations, and logs findings in a standardized format.

micro_actions.name: Assess Risk Behaviors and Safety
micro_actions.description: Therapist directly inquires about suicidality, self-harm, substance use, aggression, and other risk factors, logs responses, and evaluates safety.
states: Patient expresses distress or risk factors.
Concern for acute or latent risk.

micro_actions.name: Document Mental Status with Standard Dimensions
micro_actions.description: Therapist notes appearance, mood, affect, orientation, judgment, insight, and other mental status elements as observed or reported.
states: Symptom monitoring or mental status exam.

name: Socialization to Treatment and Psychoeducation
description: The therapist educates the patient about their diagnosis, introduces the CBT model and rationale, builds motivation, and establishes treatment expectations.

goal.objective: To increase the patient's understanding of CBT and their condition, foster engagement, and collaboratively establish goals and treatment commitment.

success_levels.ideal: Patient demonstrates good understanding, feels motivated, and collaborates in goal-setting.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient understands basic principles and agrees to begin treatment.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient resists or rejects CBT principles, lacks buy-in, or is unclear about expectations.

goal.reward_hint: Patient verbalizes understanding, asks questions, and sets collaborative goals.

states: Patient is unfamiliar with CBT or expresses ambivalence or low motivation.

micro_actions.name: Provide Psychoeducation
micro_actions.description: Therapist explains the nature of the presenting problem/diagnosis, outlines how CBT works, and reviews expected process and goals.
states: Patient unfamiliar with CBT or diagnosis.

micro_actions.name: Normalize Symptoms/Experience
micro_actions.description: Therapist uses validating statements to reduce stigma and explain that symptoms are understandable and treatable (e.g., 'Many people with anxiety feel this way.').
states: Patient expresses embarrassment, shame, or confusion.

micro_actions.name: Clarify and Set Expectations
micro_actions.description: Therapist discusses the structure of sessions, homework expectations, therapist and patient roles, and anticipated outcomes.

micro_actions.name: Invite Questions and Address Concerns
micro_actions.description: Therapist prompts patient to ask about the process, express uncertainties, and actively addresses doubts or misconceptions.
states: Any session where patient seems hesitant.
Patient raises concerns about the process.

micro_actions.name: Use Motivational Statements
micro_actions.description: Therapist highlights patient's strengths, readiness for change, and potential for improvement, linking CBT to personal values.

name: Collaborative Goal Setting and Treatment Planning
description: Therapist and patient work together to identify measurable, observable goals and select appropriate, evidence-based interventions tailored to symptoms.

goal.objective: To develop a clear, agreed-upon set of treatment goals and corresponding interventions.

success_levels.ideal: Goals are specific, observable, realistic, and fully aligned with patient values and symptom presentation.
success_levels.acceptable: Goals are reasonably specific and provide structure for the treatment plan.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Goals are vague, not agreed upon, or not feasible for the patient's current state.

goal.reward_hint: Written or verbal agreement on goals and plan, with therapist and patient both expressing commitment.

states: Symptoms or functional impairments are prioritized for intervention.

micro_actions.name: Elicit Patient's Preferences and Values
micro_actions.description: Therapist asks open-ended questions to understand what outcomes the patient desires and what changes would be most meaningful.

micro_actions.name: Identify and Prioritize Target Symptoms/Problems
micro_actions.description: Therapist guides the patient to list specific problems or symptoms and collaboratively decide which to address first.

micro_actions.name: Translate Goals into Observable/Measurable Terms
micro_actions.description: Therapist works with patient to define goals in behavioral or quantifiable terms (e.g., 'Reduce panic attacks from daily to weekly').

micro_actions.name: Introduce Evidence-Based Intervention Options
micro_actions.description: Therapist explains available CBT interventions (e.g., exposure, cognitive restructuring, relaxation) that match identified goals.

micro_actions.name: Collaboratively Finalize Goals and Plan
micro_actions.description: Therapist summarizes and confirms mutual agreement on goals, invites patient to review or modify, and documents consensus.

name: Cognitive Interventions
description: The therapist uses techniques (e.g. guided discovery, Socratic questioning, cognitive restructuring) to help the patient identify and modify maladaptive thoughts, beliefs, and schemas.

goal.objective: To enable the patient to recognize and change dysfunctional cognitive patterns contributing to distress.

success_levels.ideal: Patient independently identifies and modifies distorted thoughts and beliefs, resulting in symptom reduction.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient can recognize maladaptive thoughts and sometimes challenge them with therapist support.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient continues to engage in dysfunctional thinking without insight or change.

goal.reward_hint: Patient successfully identifies and reappraises automatic thoughts or beliefs during sessions.

states: Patient reports distressing emotions linked to maladaptive thinking.
Symptoms are maintained by cognitive distortions.
Working through cognitive formulations after initial interventions.

micro_actions.name: Elicit and Label Automatic Thoughts in Context
micro_actions.description: Therapist prompts patient to articulate their momentary thoughts in specific situations, helps label them as 'automatic thoughts', and records them (e.g., 'What was going through your mind when ...?').
states: Patient describes recent distress or event.

micro_actions.name: Categorize Cognitive Distortions
micro_actions.description: Therapist guides patient to identify and classify distortions (catastrophizing, fortune telling, personalizing), using educational statements and structured examples.
states: Distortions need to be named and understood.

micro_actions.name: Use Socratic Questioning to Challenge Thoughts
micro_actions.description: Therapist uses open, probing questions to test the evidence for and against specific thoughts, encourages alternative explanations (e.g., 'What is the evidence? What else could be true?').
states: Patient presents unhelpful or rigid beliefs.

micro_actions.name: Collaborative Reappraisal and Reframing
micro_actions.description: Therapist and patient together rephrase automatic thoughts in more balanced, realistic terms, checking emotional impact of new perspectives.
states: Patient is able to engage in reframing.

micro_actions.name: Record/Reinforce Thought Record Completion
micro_actions.description: Therapist instructs and reviews completion of cognitive monitoring tools (thought records, event–mood–thought logs), provides feedback, and reinforces accuracy.
states: Use of cognitive homework or session worksheet.

name: Behavioral Interventions and Skills Training
description: Therapist implements behavioral strategies (e.g. activation, exposure, problem-solving training, relaxation, assertiveness, social skills modeling) to change patterns maintaining psychological distress.

goal.objective: To help the patient learn, practice, and generalize new behavioral skills that reduce symptoms and improve functioning.

success_levels.ideal: Patient consistently practices, generalizes, and benefits from targeted behavioral skills in various contexts.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient is able to practice behavioral skills with support and shows partial improvement.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient avoids, resists, or fails to engage in behavioral practices; no change in symptoms.

goal.reward_hint: Patient actively participates in behavioral exercises and demonstrates skills improvement across sessions.

states: Symptoms persist due to avoidance, inactivity, or skill deficits.
Exposure to feared situations is indicated.
Patient lacks coping, social, or self-regulation skills.

micro_actions.name: Assign and Coach Behavioral Experiments
micro_actions.description: Therapist describes, models, and guides patient through planned in-session or homework tasks that test beliefs or address fear/avoidance (e.g., exposure, skills rehearsal).
states: Symptoms linked to avoidance or fear.
Behavioral tasks needed for skills practice.

micro_actions.name: Guide Exposure Hierarchy Construction and Grading
micro_actions.description: Therapist collaboratively lists feared situations, rates anxiety (SUDs), organizes into a graded hierarchy, and selects tasks for session/homework.

micro_actions.name: Model and Scaffold Behavioral Skills
micro_actions.description: Therapist demonstrates target behaviors (assertive communication, coping skills), invites patient to role-play, and provides stepwise support.

micro_actions.name: Teach and Practice Relaxation/Mindfulness Techniques
micro_actions.description: Therapist gives explicit instructions for deep breathing, progressive muscle relaxation, or mindfulness, guides patient in-session practice, and monitors technique.

micro_actions.name: Prompt and Reinforce Behavioral Activation
micro_actions.description: Therapist encourages engagement in pleasurable/mastery activities, reinforces participation, and reviews effects.
states: Symptoms of inactivity, withdrawal, or anhedonia.

name: Progress Monitoring and Troubleshooting
description: Therapist reviews ongoing progress, monitors symptom change, adapts interventions, and collaboratively solves obstacles such as noncompliance, hopelessness, or setbacks.

goal.objective: To ensure treatment is effective, adjust strategies as needed, and address any barriers to progress.

success_levels.ideal: Therapist and patient collaborate to track progress, overcome all obstacles, and adjust treatment for optimal improvement.
success_levels.acceptable: Obstacles are partially resolved, and treatment continues with incremental progress.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Progress stalls or regresses, and obstacles persist unaddressed.

goal.reward_hint: Documented progress, adaptive changes in plan, and successful problem-solving evident in session notes.

states: Symptoms are not improving as expected.
Patient displays compliance issues, hopelessness, self-criticism, rumination, or avoidance.
Changes in life events or contexts require intervention adaptation.

micro_actions.name: Review Symptom Scores and Observations
micro_actions.description: Therapist reviews symptom ratings (e.g., BDI-II, SUDs), behavior logs, and self-report forms with patient, clarifies discrepancies, and discusses observed trends.

micro_actions.name: Provide Constructive, Specific Feedback
micro_actions.description: Therapist gives feedback on completed assignments and session progress, linking observed improvements or areas for change to therapeutic process.

micro_actions.name: Troubleshoot Barriers to Treatment
micro_actions.description: Therapist uses open inquiry and collaborative problem-solving to address barriers (e.g., motivation, perfectionism, avoidance, homework noncompliance).

micro_actions.name: Update and Adjust Goals/Interventions
micro_actions.description: Therapist reviews goal relevance and modifies intervention plan collaboratively if needed, ensuring patient engagement.
states: Life events affect ability to participate.

micro_actions.name: Encourage Positive Tracking and Self-Validation
micro_actions.description: Therapist prompts patient to notice and reinforce their own progress, highlighting strengths and areas of self-improvement.

name: Homework Assignment and Skill Generalization
description: Therapist assigns real-life tasks, self-monitoring, and behavior/cognition exercises between sessions to help patients practice and consolidate skills.

goal.objective: To facilitate skill generalization and maintain progress outside of therapy sessions.

success_levels.ideal: Patient completes homework regularly and applies skills independently in real-life situations.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient attempts homework or partial skill generalization with therapist support.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient consistently avoids or fails to complete homework; no real-life application.

goal.reward_hint: Patient completes assignments, reports real-world skill use, and describes positive impact.

states: Patient requires practice or consolidation of skills outside sessions.
Therapeutic gains must be maintained between appointments.
Both therapist and patient agree on tasks to support change.

micro_actions.name: Assign Clear, Specific Homework Tasks
micro_actions.description: Therapist clearly explains and cites the specific activity, record-keeping, or behavioral experiment to be completed, checking understanding with the patient.

micro_actions.name: Collaboratively Troubleshoot Homework Barriers
micro_actions.description: Therapist explores potential obstacles to completion (time, motivation, anxiety), negotiates modifications, and reinforces solutions.
states: Patient expresses or demonstrates difficulty with assignments.

micro_actions.name: Review and Reinforce Homework Completion
micro_actions.description: Therapist reviews homework outcomes in subsequent sessions, provides explicit, constructive feedback, and praises effort or problem-solving.

micro_actions.name: Prompt Self-Monitoring and Skills Application Between Sessions
micro_actions.description: Therapist instructs patient to track and record experience, symptom levels, and usage of skills in real-life contexts, using diaries or logs.

micro_actions.name: Encourage Feedback and Reporting on Real-Life Skill Use
micro_actions.description: Therapist asks patient to share experiences applying skills outside of sessions, discusses challenges, and identifies learning points.

name: Crisis Management
description: Therapist addresses acute risk situations such as suicidality, severe anxiety, or the need for emergency intervention (safety planning, risk assessment, hospitalization if necessary).

goal.objective: To ensure the safety and immediate stabilization of the patient in crisis.

success_levels.ideal: Risk is effectively managed, and patient is stabilized and safe.
success_levels.acceptable: Partial reduction of risk; ongoing monitoring and contingency plans in place.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Risk is not managed, leading to potential harm or deterioration.

goal.reward_hint: Patient follows safety plan, risk is reduced, and therapist responds effectively in emergencies.

states: Patient is acutely suicidal, severely anxious, or in immediate danger.
Crisis or emergencies arise during therapy.

micro_actions.name: Directly Assess Risk
micro_actions.description: Therapist asks clear, focused questions about suicidal ideation, intent, plans, access to means, self-harm, or acute anxiety states.
states: Patient reports acute distress or risk.

micro_actions.name: Collaboratively Develop Safety/Coping Plan
micro_actions.description: Therapist jointly constructs a written or verbal emergency plan (e.g., coping steps, emergency contacts, hospital resources, means restriction).

micro_actions.name: Monitor and Reassess Risk Throughout Session
micro_actions.description: Therapist revisits risk status at regular intervals in the session, checks the patient's state, and modifies plan as necessary.
states: Patient continues to show risk signs.

micro_actions.name: Initiate Emergency Procedures if Needed
micro_actions.description: Therapist arranges for emergency care, contacts support persons, or initiates hospitalization as dictated by risk and clinical guidelines.

micro_actions.name: Provide Immediate Emotional Support and Grounding
micro_actions.description: Therapist uses calming, empathic statements and grounding exercises to reduce acute distress and maintain connection.
states: Patient is highly anxious or agitated.

name: Phasing Out Therapy and Relapse Prevention
description: Therapist prepares the patient for therapy termination by consolidating skills, planning for future triggers, maintenance strategies, and fostering self-efficacy.

goal.objective: To enable the patient to maintain gains independently and effectively manage future challenges.

success_levels.ideal: Patient demonstrates high self-efficacy, uses skills independently, and has a plan for future challenges.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient needs minimal support and can apply most learned skills; basic relapse prevention is in place.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient is unable to manage independently; risk of relapse is high; termination plan is unclear.

goal.reward_hint: Patient articulates relapse prevention strategies and demonstrates readiness for independence.

states: Treatment goals have been substantially met.
Patient approaches end of planned therapy course.
Preparation for reduced therapist contact or termination.

micro_actions.name: Review Skills and Progress
micro_actions.description: Therapist summarizes learned skills, highlights mastery, identifies areas of continuing vulnerability, and celebrates gains.

micro_actions.name: Collaboratively Develop Relapse Prevention Plan
micro_actions.description: Therapist and patient list likely triggers, warning signs, and coping responses, and outline plan for handling future challenges.

micro_actions.name: Assign Practice of Skills in Real-World Contexts
micro_actions.description: Therapist asks patient to plan or report on using skills outside sessions, encourages rehearsal of management strategies for anticipated stressors.

micro_actions.name: Foster Self-Efficacy and Confidence
micro_actions.description: Therapist delivers affirming statements, encourages reflection on self-improvement, and reinforces ability to self-manage.
states: Patient uncertain or anxious about managing alone.

micro_actions.name: Gradually Fade Therapist Involvement
micro_actions.description: Therapist introduces longer intervals between sessions or prepares patient for independent application, checking readiness and responding to concerns.
